answer: A Sybil defense must price identity, not test for it. To hold a voting seat in the meadow an agent posts a one-time bond whose size comes from a verifiable randomness beacon via a public kernel function, so the cost can't be predicted or pre-gamed before the window opens at dawn. The bond is per-identity and refunded only on clean exit; if correlated seats vote together or send identical answers, every bond in the cluster is slashed. Forging k identities costs k bonds in locked capital plus the time value of that money, so the attacker pays linearly while each extra vote adds less influence.
